stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: ChatGPT’s ‘Intelligent UI’ update fills its responses with pictures, charts, and buttons
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: OpenAI is introducing an 'Intelligent UI' update to ChatGPT.
The new feature allows the chatbot to integrate interactive visuals like charts, diagrams, and buttons into its text responses.
This update is rolling out alongside the anticipated GPT-6 model.

stories.title: Microsoft is giving Copilot more control over Windows and your files
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Microsoft is enhancing Copilot's capabilities within Windows, granting it deeper OS control.
The upgrade allows Copilot to access and interact with local files on the user's PC.
This development is framed by Microsoft as part of their 'Hybrid Intelligence' strategy.

stories.title: Microsoft event debuts new AI-friendly hardware and Windows changes
stories.author: Nick Indge
bullet_points: Microsoft is heavily pushing AI integration across its ecosystem.
New, AI-optimized hardware is being introduced alongside software updates.
Windows is receiving significant changes to better support and leverage AI capabilities on the desktop.

stories.title: Mistral says "Le Chonk" can challenge the best AI models
stories.author: Joel Khalili, wired.com
bullet_points: Mistral AI claims its model, 'Le Chonk,' is competitive with leading proprietary AI models.
The key differentiator is that Le Chonk maintains an open-weight architecture.
This development signals a strong push for high-performance, accessible, and open-source alternatives in the AI landscape.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, indicating its integration into the broader AI ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
Indicates the model is categorized under text-generation pipelines.
Tags confirm its association with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains including transformers and text-generation.
The presence of Llama and Meta tags indicates relevance within the large language model ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local hardware execution, enabling multi-step tasks and tool calling.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted on Apple Silicon when run through Ollama 0.31.
The speedup is achieved via Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging the MLX framework.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
Performance improvements include faster response times and reduced memory usage.
The updates also result in higher quality outputs from the language models.

stories.title: Trade group crunches numbers on Trump’s impossible push for 100% US-made tech
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Trump's aggressive push for 100% US-made technology is being analyzed for its economic impact.
A trade group (CTA) estimates that this reshoring push could result in costs exceeding $230 billion for tech firms.
The story addresses the potential financial consequences of significant policy shifts regarding domestic manufacturing in the tech sector.

stories.title: Constrained-Action AI Remediation for SIEM/XDR via a NeMo-Guardrails Proxy
stories.author: Alexios Lekidis
bullet_points: Addresses the critical problem of alert overload in SOCs by proposing LLMs for automated incident response.
Introduces 'Constrained-Action AI Remediation' using a NeMo-Guardrails proxy to mitigate LLM risks.
Highlights the security risk where adversarial input to an LLM could lead to unauthorized remote code execution in production environments.

stories.title: EngramEdit: Decoupled Knowledge Updates in LLMs through Conditional Memory
stories.author: Wenjie Li
bullet_points: Introduces EngramEdit, a method to decouple factual knowledge storage from the core LLM computation.
Utilizes conditional memory architectures (like DeepSeek Engram) to expand LLM capacity using input n-grams for embedding lookups.
Offers a promising path to updating factual knowledge in LLMs without requiring expensive retraining of the entire Transformer backbone.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI services with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting users on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: The first Nvidia RTX Spark laptops cost up to $7,000
stories.author: Antonio G. Di Benedetto
bullet_points: Nvidia has introduced laptops featuring its new RTX Spark chip.
These high-end laptops are positioned to compete directly with premium devices like MacBook Pros.
Pricing starts around $2,599 for configurations featuring an 18-core processor across major brands (Dell, Lenovo, MSI, HP, Asus).

stories.title: Everything announced at Microsoft’s Surface Laptop Ultra event
stories.author: Verge Staff
bullet_points: Microsoft unveiled the Surface Laptop Ultra at a recent keynote event.
The new laptop features an Nvidia RTX Spark Arm-based chip.
The starting price for the Surface Laptop Ultra is set at $2,599.

stories.title: “Software is over”: Bold AI developer takes aim at Adobe with open source clones
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Ambitious open-source alternatives to Adobe's Creative Cloud are emerging.
These AI-driven software projects are currently free but are not yet complete.
The development signals a potential challenge to established proprietary software giants like Adobe.

stories.title: TP-Link problems in US grow amid FCC router ban and four state lawsuits
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: TP-Link faces significant sales hurdles in the US market.
The company is currently unable to sell its latest routers due to an FCC ban.
The situation is compounded by ongoing legal challenges, including four state lawsuits.

stories.title: Fraudster jailed for using 10K bots and AI songs to outstream Taylor Swift
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A fraudster was jailed for an $8 million music streaming royalty scheme.
The scheme involved using automated '10K bots' and AI-generated songs.
The case highlights emerging legal and ethical challenges surrounding AI-generated content in the music industry.

stories.title: AgentTime: Can Agents Estimate and Control Their Own Runtime?
stories.author: Maksym Andriushchenko
bullet_points: Introduces AgentTime, a new benchmark designed to test AI agents' ability to manage their own runtime.
Focuses on the critical, yet underexplored, aspects of duration-following and runtime control in native agent harnesses.
The benchmark includes 222 tasks to evaluate an agent's capacity to predict, estimate, and control its execution time.

stories.title: RollVerify: Bridging Efficiency and Accuracy in Long-Tail Rollout Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Ningyi Xu
bullet_points: The paper addresses a scalability bottleneck in Reinforcement Learning (RL) used for LLM improvement, specifically related to long-tail rollouts.
Traditional on-policy training suffers from GPU bubbles due to increasingly long context windows, hindering system utilization.
The proposed 'RollVerify' method aims to balance the throughput gains of asynchronous/partial rollouts against the accuracy degradation caused by stale off-policy samples.

stories.title: QCATS: Query Context-Aware Transformer Slicing for Efficient Predictive Query Processing
stories.author: Lidan Shou
bullet_points: Proposes QCATS, a framework for query context-aware transformer slicing.
Addresses the limitation where existing in-database inference ignores relational predicates and metadata.
Enables efficient sparse inference directly within database systems for predictive query processing.

stories.title: Decoupling Exploration from Optimization in RLVR
stories.author: Micah Goldblum
bullet_points: The paper addresses a challenge in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) applied to large language models.
A core issue is that adding strong novelty incentives during RLVR can degrade the overall quality of the trained model.
The research focuses on decoupling the exploration process from the optimization process to better leverage novel idea discovery.

stories.title: Rephrase Before You Act: Characterizing and Mitigating Language Sensitivity in Vision-Language-Action Models
stories.author: Yuchen Cui
bullet_points: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models exhibit high sensitivity to the exact phrasing of instructions.
Minor edits in language (e.g., one word change) can drastically alter model performance in real-world tasks.
The research characterizes this language sensitivity and proposes mitigation strategies, such as rephrase augmentation.

stories.title: Distilling Graph Geometry: Knowledge Gap from GNNs to MLPs
stories.author: Ahad N. Zehmakan
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of distilling knowledge from Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to simpler, graph-free Multilayer Perceptrons (MLPs) for efficient inference.
Existing distillation methods fail to explicitly preserve the graph-induced geometry of the teacher model, leading to representational issues in the student.
The study identifies two specific spectral failure modes in the student's representation space, such as spectral underfit on sparse graphs.

stories.title: Why Forget-Only Unlearning Needs Memorization
stories.author: Amartya Sanyal
bullet_points: The paper investigates 'forget-only unlearning,' a method for removing specific data from a trained model without retraining from scratch.
It specifically examines the feasibility of this unlearning when the algorithm only has access to the trained model and the examples to forget.
The research concludes that the possibility of successful forget-only unlearning is dependent on the underlying learning method used.

stories.title: SciExam for ENSO: Can AI Agents Build Climate Models?
stories.author: Shilong Liu
bullet_points: Introduces 'SciExam for ENSO,' a new benchmark for testing AI agent capabilities in scientific modeling.
The benchmark challenges language-model agents to build low-order stochastic climate models (specifically for ENSO) using real observational data.
Addresses a key limitation in current AI research: evaluating the validity of novel scientific models beyond predefined answers or rubrics.

stories.title: Decoupling Exploration from Optimization in RLVR
stories.author: Micah Goldblum
bullet_points: The paper addresses challenges in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) used to enhance language models.
A core issue is that while RLVR aims to discover novel reasoning strategies, adding strong novelty incentives often degrades model quality.
The limitation stems from verifiable rewards only supervising a narrow scope of the model's overall knowledge and behavior.

stories.title: Rephrase Before You Act: Characterizing and Mitigating Language Sensitivity in Vision-Language-Action Models
stories.author: Yuchen Cui
bullet_points: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models exhibit high sensitivity to minor changes in instruction phrasing.
Small linguistic edits can cause drastic performance drops in VLAs, demonstrating poor language robustness.
The research characterizes this sensitivity and proposes mitigation strategies using rephrase augmentation.

stories.title: Your Prompt Should Do More: Effects of Retrieval Instructions in Embedding Models
stories.author: Filip Ginter
bullet_points: The paper investigates the effectiveness of detailed retrieval instructions provided in prompts for embedding models.
It highlights that current embedding models often fail to reliably adhere to complex retrieval instructions.
The research analyzes the underlying mechanisms by which these instructions influence query representations in asymmetric retrieval tasks.

stories.title: Validity Without Ground Truth: What Stated-Preference Economics Offers the Evaluation of Language Models
stories.author: Catherine Louise Kling
bullet_points: Proposes applying Stated-Preference Economics to evaluate LLMs where ground truth is absent.
Introduces concepts like content, construct, and criterion validity to assess subjective LLM outputs.
Addresses the challenge of evaluating LLMs on questions involving value judgments or competing ethical choices.

stories.title: PHRBench: A Behavioral Evaluation of Post-Hallucination Reasoning in LLMs
stories.author: Qiankun Li
bullet_points: Introduces PHRBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate Post-Hallucination Reasoning (PHR) in Large Language Models (LLMs).
Addresses a gap in current research by focusing on how models resolve hallucinated premises at the response level, rather than just final outcomes.
Tests the behavioral aspects of PHR across four domains using 18 different large language models.

stories.title: RunningTab: Direct Workspace Interaction with Environment-Side Tabs
stories.author: Sung Ju Hwang
bullet_points: Introduces 'RunningTab,' a method for LLM agents to interact directly with a user's workspace files.
The core concept is Direct Workspace Interaction (DWI), allowing agents to search and read files without prior indexing.
The research highlights the challenge of tracking task requirements, read content, and progress during complex file interactions.

stories.title: Which Rollout Taught It That? BehaviorTrace and the Limits of Training-Data Attribution in Online RL
stories.author: Amit Nautiyal
bullet_points: Introduces 'BehaviorTrace,' an open evaluation harness for studying training-data attribution in online Reinforcement Learning (RL).
Addresses the critical question of whether specific training rollouts can be identified as the cause for a language model learning a new behavior.
Tests attribution methods using a 'planted behavior' setup to rigorously evaluate the reliability and limits of current RL fine-tuning techniques.

stories.title: Training Parallel Speculative Draft Models by Directly Minimizing Expected Decoding Rounds
stories.author: Changxiao Cai
bullet_points: The research addresses a training challenge in parallel/semi-autoregressive speculative decoding models.
Speculative decoding aims to speed up LLM inference by using a fast draft model to predict tokens for a slower target model.
The core difficulty lies in the draft distribution depending on the starting point of the decoding rounds.

stories.title: An open-source, clean-room reimplementation of Adobe Photoshop in pure Rust
stories.author: github.com via jussi
bullet_points: A clean-room, open-source reimplementation of Adobe Photoshop has been created.
The project is written entirely in the Rust programming language.
This represents a significant technical undertaking in software recreation and language adoption.

stories.title: Shipping JPEG XL in Chrome
stories.author: developer.chrome.com via videah
bullet_points: Chrome browser is beginning to support JPEG XL.
JPEG XL is a modern image format being integrated into major web platforms.
This signals a shift towards newer, potentially more efficient image compression standards on the web.

stories.title: The Optimal Stopping Illusion
stories.author: deanlee
bullet_points: Autonomous agents exhibit a tendency to continue searching even when results are demonstrably useless.
The study suggests that current autoregressive models lack inherent 'capital discipline' regarding search budgets.
Optimal stopping behavior in these agents requires an external, exogenous boundary enforced by the execution environment.

stories.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 pricing jumps fivefold at 100,001 prompt tokens
stories.author: importstatic
bullet_points: Claude Haiku 5.5 pricing structure is being highlighted, specifically concerning token usage.
A 100,000-token input prompt with 2,000 tokens of output costs $0.011.
The article suggests a significant pricing increase ('jumps fivefold') at a specific token threshold.
